title: Couchbase, Inc.
text:
June 2010 – Membase project begins. NoSQL’s rise and the Membase launch notes the project was open-sourced in mid-2010 by memcached leaders with Zynga and NHN (now Naver).[1] WIRED

Feb 2011 – CouchOne and Membase merge to form Couchbase, Inc. [2,3] TechCrunch, eWEEK

Jan 2012 – Couchbase Server 1.8 GA. Rebranded Membase line.[4] Scribd

Dec 2012 – Couchbase Server 2.0 GA with JSON document store, distributed indexing/query, incremental MapReduce, and XDCR.[5,6] InfoQ, The Register, Database Trends and Applications

May 2014 – Couchbase Mobile 1.0. Couchbase’s mobile stack for iOS/Android with local data store and sync gateway.[7] InformationWeek

Oct 2014 – ForestDB engine announced (B+-trees). Couchbase replaces its storage engine with ForestDB for performance/transactions.[8] InfoQ

Oct 2015 – Couchbase Server 4.0 introduces multi-dimensional scaling, geospatial indexes and new query language N1QL (SQL++). SQL-like query leap.[9] InfoWorld

Dec 2015 – Couchbase Mobile 1.1. 1.1 drop (Lite & Sync Gateway enhancements).[10] Dzone

Feb 2016 – Couchbase Mobile 1.2 (enterprise-grade upgrades incl. ForestDB in Lite).[11] TDWI

Nov 2016 – Server 4.6 Developer Preview with FTS improvements, XDCR with globally ordered conflict resolution, and real-time connectors for Spark 2.0 and Kafka.[12,13] InfoQ, ADTmag

Oct 2017 – Server 5.0 GA (Full-Text Search service broad availability; ephemeral buckets).[14] Altoros

Aug 2018 – Couchbase Mobile 2.1.[15] SDTimes

Oct 2018 – Couchbase Server 6.0 GA; Analytics Service for JSON (SQL++/no-ETL) and the Kubernetes Autonomous Operator introduced around this period.[16] VentureBeat, 1PR Newswire

Apr 2019 – Couchbase Mobile 2.5 adds Predictive Query API (DP), enhanced logging, fine-grained replication events, expanded Sync Gateway monitoring.[17] VentureBeat

Jan 2020 – Server 6.5 adds distributed ACID transactions; Mobile 2.7/SG 2.7. 6.5 momentum.[18] TechTarget

Jul 2020 – “Couchbase Cloud” (later Capella) GA on AWS. Managed DBaaS launch.[19] VentureBeat

Aug 2020 – Server 6.6 GA. Performance and manageability updates.[20] VentureBeat

Jul 2021 – Server 7.0 GA, fusing NoSQL flexibility with relational concepts (collections/scopes, SQL transactions).[21] The Register

Oct/Nov 2021 – Capella (managed DBaaS) launch/branding on AWS.[22] CRN

Oct 2021 – Couchbase Lite 3.0 & Sync Gateway 3.0 (C API for broader devices, SQL++ on mobile).[23] GitHub

June 2022 – Capella on Google Cloud. Multi-cloud expansion.[24] IoT Now

Jan 19, 2023 – Capella on Microsoft Azure.[25] InfoWorld

Nov/Dec 2023 – Capella Analytics (a.k.a. Columnar) announced.[26] forums.theregister.com, Database Trends and Applications

Mar 2024 – Server 7.6 GA adds Vector Search & SQL++ enhancements. Vector search across Server/Capella.[27] Blocks and Files

Aug 2024 – Couchbase Lite 3.2 & Sync Gateway 3.3 (LTS) with vector search integration. Mobile/edge vector search availability.[28] Blocks and Files

Dec 2, 2024 – Capella AI Services: independent coverage details Model Service (LLM hosting), Vectorization, Unstructured Data Service, AI Agent Catalog, and AI Functions for SQL++.[29,30] SiliconANGLE, TechTarget, CRN

Jan & May 2025 – 7.6.x maintenance (7.6.5/7.6.6). Community version trackers reflect current 7.6.x release.[17] VentureBeat

Feb 24–25, 2025 – NVIDIA NIM integration.[31,32] TechTarget, Channel Insider

Mar 4, 2025 – Couchbase Edge Server 1.0 GA (lightweight, offline-first, ~1 GB RAM target).[33,34,35] The New Stackedgeir.com, DEVOPSdigest, Database Trends and Applications

July 2025 – Capella listed in the new AWS Marketplace “AI Agents & Tools” category. See AWS Marketplace listing and third-party trade coverage of the new category and Capella’s availability.[36,37] Amazon Web Services, Inc.Channel Insider, DEVOPSdigest
